proof_assessment.supplier58: Both complete current proofs reread and byte-identical to prior focused Ville snapshots. Finite-horizon first hitting time truncated at N is bounded; a*1_A <= stopped value almost surely, hence aP(A)<=E M_0. Increasing horizons bound actual crossing; gamma_n decreasing to alpha yields strictly lower thresholds increasing to 1/alpha, their crossing intersection equals the supremum event. No attainment assumption.
proof_assessment.consumer_theorem: Statement and proof steps unchanged. F4 now names the exact authored run-local Ville theorem and its actual supremum bound. For each fixed theta, current mixture theorem supplies a nonnegative test supermartingale under singleton P_theta, AC and initial value 1. Closed-interval exclusion implies |S_t|>u_alpha, hence threshold crossing by current equivalence lemma; the exclusion union is contained in the measurable supremum event. Ville bounds that event by alpha. Membership measurability and C_0=Theta complete confidence-sequence definition.
proof_assessment.consumer_example: Byte-identical to prior observation. Gaussian mixture integral with rho_prime=1/tau_squared,v=0,s=lambda gives the finite normal mgf. Borel transformation preserves the displayed independence identity, so the inspected independent-variable lemma applies to exp(lambda Y_t). Conditional mgf <=exp(lambda_squared*sigma_squared/2) follows from sigma_squared>=tau_squared. Adaptedness and common discrete filtration meet theorem interface, with pointwise parameter coverage and AC carried in Facts and verification.
proof_assessment.local_mixture_suppliers: Complete local bodies inspected: component integrability follows bounded truncation plus monotone convergence; integrable taking-out-known gives one-step supermartingale. Product-measurable exponential family meets inspected published mixture theorem; Tonelli does not require one common exceptional set over all lambda. Local normal square-completion integral is finite for rho>0,v>=0 and real S_t, so no infinite-mixture modification occurs. Boundary equivalence keeps closed threshold and strict interval exclusion correctly distinct.
